rules.statement: A doc comment that describes a limit must state the limit the code actually enforces, and must not claim it covers cases the code rejects.
rules.why: A caller who trusts an overstated comment hits an ArgumentOutOfRangeException the comment said would not happen.
rules.check: Compare doc-comment claims about maximums and ranges with the comparisons in the code, including edge cases such as a leap-year window plus an allowance.

rules.statement: In a test project, test an upper or lower bound at exactly the limit (succeeds) and one unit past it (fails), not only far beyond it.
rules.why: Without boundary cases, changing `>` to `>=` in the check would still pass the tests.
rules.check: For each range check under test, look for a case at exactly the limit and one a tick or unit over it. Tests that only use values far outside the range don't count.

rules.statement: Don't ask a contracts-only `*.Abstractions` data type to reject duplicate entries across a set when the set is validated as a whole where it is composed at startup.
rules.why: Abstractions assemblies hold contracts and data only, and the conventions validate a registered set when it is composed, where the offending name can be reported.
rules.check: Before reporting missing duplicate checks in an abstractions type, find out whether a composition or registration step validates the set as a whole.

rules.statement: In a test project, a test that expects an ArgumentException (including ArgumentNullException) must also assert the exception's `ParamName`.
rules.why: A check on a different argument could throw the same exception type and the test would still pass.
rules.check: Look for Assert.Throws on argument exceptions where the test never checks `ParamName`.

rules.statement: In a test project, put tests of a type's members in that type's test class, so that each test file mirrors one type under test.
rules.why: Someone looking for a member's coverage in its type's test file won't find it anywhere else, and the file stops mirroring one type.
rules.check: Look for test regions or methods that exercise a member of a type other than the one the test class is named for.

rules.statement: Don't report `new` object-creation expressions passed as arguments, such as an expected value built inline in an assertion, as violating the rule against calls nested in other calls' arguments: that rule covers method calls only.
rules.why: The maintainers read the hoisting rule as covering method calls, not object creation.
rules.check: Report a nested call only when it is a method invocation inside another call's arguments, not a `new` expression.

rules.statement: Wrap doc-comment lines at the width the rest of the file keeps (about 120 columns), as sibling `<param>` tags do.
rules.why: A single overlong line breaks the wrap width the file otherwise keeps.
rules.check: Look for `///` lines noticeably longer than about 120 columns when the rest of the file wraps.

rules.statement: Don't ask for invariant-culture formatting of numbers interpolated into exception messages meant for people: the invariant-culture rule covers values formatted or parsed for machines.
rules.why: Exception messages are for people, the build's analyzers (CA1305) don't flag them, and a positive int formats the same in every .NET culture.
rules.check: Before reporting culture-sensitive formatting, check whether the string is a human-facing message or a value a machine formats or parses.

rules.statement: Don't report a private constructor with more than three parameters when its only callers are adjacent one-line factories that each set one value, and tests assert the values left unset.
rules.why: The parameter guideline says "rarely more than three". One constructor per kind would add members to guard against a swap the factory tests already catch.
rules.check: Before reporting a long parameter list, check whether the constructor is private, which factories call it, and whether tests cover each factory's unused values.

rules.statement: Don't ask wire-value string constants that peers match ordinally to be composed from other constants: keep each one a whole literal that can be read and searched.
rules.why: A wire value is matched exactly by providers and consumers. A test that pins each prefix catches drift.
rules.check: Before reporting repeated prefixes in string constants, check whether they are protocol or wire values and whether a test pins them.

rules.statement: Don't ask a small validated immutable value type to become a `readonly record struct` when its `default` instance would bypass constructor validation, but do expect a `//` comment on the type saying why it is a class.
rules.why: A struct's default instance skips the constructor, so invalid values could reach consumers. As classes, every instance has passed validation.
rules.check: For a sealed record class holding a small value, check whether its constructor validates and whether a comment or ADR explains choosing a class. Report only when the comment is missing.

rules.statement: A comment on an analyzer suppression or a package/build workaround must name the tracking issue or ADR and say when the workaround can be removed.
rules.why: Otherwise a later maintainer can't tell whether the workaround is still needed after the dependency or SDK changes.
rules.check: Look at new suppressions in .editorconfig, Directory.Packages.props and project files, and at workaround comments, for an issue or ADR reference and a removal condition.

rules.statement: Don't report a CHANGELOG `### Security` entry that describes dependency or supply-chain checks as misfiled: under the template's changelog convention, Security holds the package's security posture and protections.
rules.why: Checking every dependency that ships, transitive ones included, is part of the supply-chain posture a consumer can rely on. Added holds capabilities of the package itself.
rules.check: Check the changelog convention (template ADR-0015) before asking for a Security entry to be moved.

rules.statement: Don't ask a citation of a project-template ADR to carry a `project-template` prefix: project records are numbered from 1000 and template records below it, so an ADR number names one record across both folders.
rules.why: The numbering scheme makes a bare ADR number unambiguous, and the link points into the template folder.
rules.check: Check the ADR number range and the link target before reporting an ambiguous ADR citation.

rules.statement: Don't report a decision record for restating another record when it cites that record and summarizes what it settles in one clause to frame what this record adds.
rules.why: A one-clause summary next to a citation tells the reader what this record adds. It doesn't copy the other record's rule terms.
rules.check: Report restatement only when the record repeats another record's rule terms, not when it cites the record with a brief summary.

rules.statement: Don't ask for Markdown table columns to be re-padded when the repository runs no Markdown formatter.
rules.why: Nothing will rewrite the table later, and re-padding every row turns each future entry into a whole-table diff. The table renders correctly as it is.
rules.check: Check whether the repository's formatters (for example CSharpier, which formats only C# and XML) cover Markdown before reporting table alignment.
